roster-unicode-15-1-arm-kind.reason: Adopt for #206, part of #154, by the repository owner's direction for #154, delegated through the migration's orchestration on 2026-10-19. Diagnostics keep the program name roster.py. Records an intended difference from older interpreters. Old behavior: roster.py, now retired, quoted it through the running interpreter's repr, so it escaped characters that interpreter's Unicode database lacked: on Python 3.12 or older the diagnostic spelled U+2EBF0 as \U0002ebf0. New behavior: bench-tools roster quotes through pytext::repr, which escapes exactly the code points Python 3.14's str.isprintable() rejects (Unicode 16.0), unassigned ones included, checked against Python 3.14 for every code point. Rationale: a pinned result that does not depend on the interpreter. Compatibility impact: a quoted value changes when it holds a character assigned after the former interpreter's Unicode version. Against Python 3.12, which CI uses (Unicode 15.0), that is 5,812 code points, those added in Unicode 15.1 and 16.0, which 3.12 escapes and Rust writes as-is; none the other way. Older interpreters differ on more: Python 3.13 (Unicode 15.1) on 5,185, the Unicode 16.0 additions, and Python 3.10 (Unicode 13.0) on 11,130. This case pins U+2EBF0, added in Unicode 15.1, in the unknown arm kind. Resolving issue: #206.

roster-abbreviated-root.reason: Adopt for #215 slice A, part of #149, under #154's authority: the repository owner allowed pinned crates.io dependencies in rust/bench-tools on 2026-10-19, and #215 replaces main.rs's hand-written option parsing with clap 4.6.7 (derive, infer_long_args), delegated through the migration's orchestration on 2026-10-19. Diagnostics keep the program name roster.py. Changes accepted input on purpose. Old behavior: bench-tools roster matched a long option only when spelled in full and refused a prefix such as --ro as an unrecognized argument, exit 2. New behavior: clap's infer_long_args expands a unique prefix of a long option, as argparse does; an ambiguous prefix is still a usage error, exit 2. Rationale: #215 asks for argparse-style abbreviations through infer_long_args. Compatibility impact: command lines that spell options in full are unchanged, and a unique prefix that was refused now runs, toward Python: the deleted bench/tools/roster.py accepted the prefix too under Python 3.12 and 3.14. Resolving issue: #215.

roster-dot-digit-root.reason: Adopt for #215 slice A, part of #149, under #154's authority: the repository owner allowed pinned crates.io dependencies in rust/bench-tools on 2026-10-19, and #215 replaces main.rs's hand-written option parsing with clap 4.6.7 (derive, infer_long_args), delegated through the migration's orchestration on 2026-10-19. Diagnostics keep the program name roster.py. Changes accepted input on purpose. Old behavior: a value made of a dash, digits and dots, such as -.5, was read as a value, as argparse reads a negative number. New behavior: clap 4.6.7 reads a dash-led argument as a value only when it parses as a number with a digit before any dot, so -.5 is an unexpected argument, exit 2; -5 and -1.5 remain values. Rationale: allow_negative_numbers has no setting for argparse's rule, and emulating argparse would keep the hand-written parsing #215 removes; no caller passes such a value. Compatibility impact: give the value attached, as --root=-.5, which still works; the deleted bench/tools/roster.py read -.5 as the value under Python 3.12 and 3.14. Resolving issue: #215.
